query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of manganese (Mn) to the FeCoNi alloy, forming a FeCoNiMn high-entropy alloy with an almost equiatomic composition, will increase the coercivity due to enhanced exchange interactions and lattice distortion.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNi fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and low coercive field
generation.intervention: Addition of manganese (Mn) to form FeCoNiMn high-entropy alloy
generation.conditions: Almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
generation.mechanism: Enhanced exchange interactions due to the addition of Mn with high magnetic moment and suitable valence electrons, leading to increased coercivity
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercivity increase of at least 20% relative to the FeCoNi baseline
generation.baseline: FeCoNi fcc alloy with low coercive field
generation.boundary: Configurational entropy of at least 1.0R and almost equiatomic composition
generation.uncertainty: The actual increase in coercivity may vary depending on the exact composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare FeCoNiMn high-entropy alloy samples with varying Mn content and measure their coercivity using a vibrating sample magnetometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCoNiMn alloy does not increase by at least 20% relative to the FeCoNi baseline for any Mn content above 10 at.%, the hypothesis is falsified
